root_cause_and_implementation: PART A. Direct grep of D-MD-B18-A002-005, CI-MD-B18-A002-001, and MD_B18_A002_CONSOLIDATED_REMEDIATION_PACKAGE.md for repair_candidate/incremental/createPromoteRunFromSeed/promote_mode/full_publish returns zero matches in all three -- none of them addresses this scenario. The C1 contract (MD_B18_A002_C1_PRODUCER_BOUND_INPUT_CONTRACT.md) does: Sec5's C01 row lists 'EodRunRepository::getOrCreateOwningRun, createAsKnownReplayRun, createPromoteRunFromSeed' as a producer surface C1 must capture ('A seed/promote run cannot silently inherit one snapshot while consuming another'), and the same Sec5's 'Alternate entry paths and operation inverses' subsection -- a cross-cutting list applying to every C01-C12 slot, not just C01 -- states 'The implementation slice must account for all of these before its coverage claim: ... import-only to promote through createPromoteRunFromSeed ...', and separately states the correct interim behavior directly: 'Existing flows without complete producer evidence fail closed.' F-020's own original disposition searched only for the literal strings repair_candidate/promote_mode/request_mode in that contract and found nothing, concluding (incorrectly) that no requirement existed either way; that search missed the contract's actual reference, which names the repository method (createPromoteRunFromSeed) rather than the promote-mode string. Separately, two LOCKED strategy documents -- outranking the C1 contract, which is explicitly marked Role: IMPLEMENTATION_GUIDANCE, MUTABLE_UNTIL_CLOSURE, no strategy authority -- name this scenario directly and require it to keep working: Import_Promote_Separation_Contract.md's 'Allowed request modes' lists correction_candidate as a first-class allowed mode ('repair_candidate may be accepted only for backward compatibility and must never authorize in-place repair' -- i.e. only the legacy NAME is a compatibility concession, the FUNCTION is required); and Finalize_Lock_And_Pointer_Behavior_LOCKED.md Sec3's lock-behavior mapping table states a 'Correction candidate / non-current publish target (legacy runtime may label this repair_candidate)' must reach 'SUCCESS or HELD according to existing policy', never permanently and unconditionally blocked. incremental is not a separate concept requiring separate authority search: MarketDataPipelineService::resolvePromoteContext() (MarketDataPipelineService.php:3436) and PromoteMarketDataCommand.php:147 both hard-map 'incremental' => 'repair_candidate' before any other logic runs, so every governance conclusion about one applies identically to the other. Existing tests/evidence before E038: E031-E033's 'whole-C1 completeness' proof is accurate for what it tested (runPipelineThroughHashUnsealed/runDaily, which only ever drives the normal INGEST_BARS-through-HASH sequence under one owning run_id) but never exercised the createPromoteRunFromSeed entry path C1 Sec5 already named in scope -- so the gap F-020 documents predates E038 and is a leftover incompleteness in the same C02-C09 capture work the contract already authorized, not a defect E038's orchestration wiring introduced; E038 was simply the first thing to make the pre-existing gap observable, by making the manifest check load-bearing on every real run instead of an opt-in audit tool. CLASSIFICATION: none of the four offered categories fits alone. It is NOT an implementation defect in Binding orchestration (completeHash/sealCandidatePublication behave exactly as designed for every entry path whole-C1 capture already covers). It IS authorized fail-closed behavior in the narrow sense that refusing to bind without complete producer evidence is exactly what C1 Sec5 requires while the gap is open. It IS an explicit, already-named dependency/blocker: C1 Sec5's own entry-path list already put createPromoteRunFromSeed in scope, so this is unfinished, already-authorized capture work, not a new problem. It is NOT a genuinely unresolved semantic decision about whether repair_candidate/incremental should keep working -- LOCKED authority already answers that (yes) -- what remains open is purely the implementation mechanism (capture carry-forward from the seed run, independent re-capture on the derived run, or another approach), which this audit does not decide or implement. NET EFFECT ON E038: E038's claim 'Binding (C1 contract Sec6 step 2) is now fully complete' overstated scope. The orchestration mechanism E038 built is complete and correct. C1 Sec5's own coverage-claim condition ('must account for all of these before its coverage claim') was not met, because createPromoteRunFromSeed was never proven and is now proven not to satisfy whole-C1 capture completeness. E038 itself is not edited (IMMUTABLE_AFTER_ISSUE); this record supersedes its completeness claim with the precise one below. ARE THE TWO markTestSkipped() CALLS LEGITIMATE CLOSURE? No. They encoded 'blocked pending a decision this attempt has no authority to make' -- a premise this audit shows is wrong on both halves: there is no undecided whether (LOCKED authority requires it to work), and the interim fail-closed behavior is not an open question either (C1 Sec5 already requires it). SKIP therefore suppressed visibility of an active regression against LOCKED authority rather than recording an understood, authorized interim state. The correct disposition -- replacing both skips with assertions that positively prove the current, contractually-required fail-closed outcome, the same treatment E038 already gave test_binding_rejects_an_incomplete_capture_manifest -- is not performed in this audit-only turn per the user's explicit no-new-coding instruction for this turn; it is recorded as the immediate next test-correctness action, separate from the larger capture-completeness implementation decision. PART B. E032 (SQLite-only whole-C1 audit, prior to any Binding wiring) explicitly declined to seed the SQLite mirror, stating doing so 'has no existing C1 capture/manifest authority behind it and was out of this audit's scope' -- correct at that time, because Binding was not wired into any live call path, so an empty eod_reason_codes in the disposable SQLite mirror was cosmetic and did not block anything real. Once E038 wired Binding into completeHash (itself already authorized by E035 under D005/CI-001, not a new decision), the same empty fixture stopped being cosmetic: it became a blocking regression across nearly the entire pre-existing SQLite-backed suite, because every test reaching HASH now genuinely needs a real registry population to pass the manifest check the same way production always has. Seeding it is therefore classified as a necessary, DERIVED consequence of an already-authorized change (wiring Binding live), not an independent new decision requiring its own fresh authorization -- directly supported by the C1 contract's own Sec4.3 ('SQLite mirror receives the required fields and behavioral fixture data', in the context of what the mirror needs for C1 verification to be meaningful at all). Content provenance was independently re-verified this audit turn, field by field (code, category, description, severity, is_active) via direct byte-level regex extraction and comparison against docs/market_data/development/implementation/db/registry/Reason_Codes_Seed.sql -- the exact same canonical file WholeC1RegistryVersionsMariaDbAuditTest and ReasonCodeSeedExecutionTest already treat as authoritative: 437/437 rows, zero mismatches on any field, zero rows only in one side. This is an exact set-and-content match, not a coincidental count match, and creates no second/competing canonical registry source.
